mei: quick heads-up — orion-v2 int4 bring-up shows weird handling of interpunct/middle-dot (U+00B7) in mixed Han+Hangul strings. small BLEU drop on loc set. repro below.

mei: example input -> "東京都·서울·駅"
mei: oracle detok -> "東京都·서울·駅"
mei: orion-v2-int4 detok -> "東京都서울·駅"  <-- missing middle-dot between kanji and hangul, runs together

ana (note): ran small eval on loc-subset (1k sentences zh/ja/ko mixed). BLEU -1.3 relative to int8 baseline, mostly where interpunct used as delimiter.

ana: stack: tokenizers v2.3.1, our detokenizer script (eng-ml/detok/loc-detok.py), quant profile int4-wtq

ana: repro snippet: ```bash
eval_local.sh --model orion-v2-int4 --subset loc-mix-1k --detok scripts/loc-detok.py
```

jun: can you paste raw tokenization for that example? curious whether token boundary got swallowed during merge.

mei: tokenized (ours): ```
['東', '京', '都', '·', '서', '울', '·', '駅']
```
mei: model tokens (from logits->ids->detok): ```
['東', '京', '都', '서', '울', '·', '駅']
```
mei: so the · moved position after decoding — looks like decoder-side merge weirdness.

sachin: hm — could be KV-cache alignment + int4 kernel rounding on mixed-script positions. we saw similar pointer shift with zero-width joiner before.

sachin: quick try: disable cache-merge for short sequences in runtime, re-run single example.

ci-bot: CI: orion-v2-int4 smoke run completed (link: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/2112233344). Detok mismatch test failed 1/120 (detok mismatch pattern: middle-dot).

ana: thanks. i'll run bisect across quantization scale (scale clipping / per-channel vs per-tensor) — could be falsy mapping of punctuation embedding.

jun: FYI here's minimal transformer decode snippet we used to inspect ids: ```python
# decode path
ids = model.generate(input_ids, max_len=32)
text = tokenizer.decode(ids, clean_up_tokenization_spaces=False)
print(repr(text))
```

mei: adding sample debug outputs to thread: ```
# input ids around dot
... 1045, 8021, 12345, 302, 897 ...  # (kanji, kanji, kanji, middle-dot, hangul)
# decoded ids -> 1045,8021,12345,897,302 ...  # dot moved after hangul in decode ordering
```

sachin: ok this smells like an attention/relative-pos index bug in int4 kernel (re-ordering of chunked kv when tokens cross script boundary at split). Not purely detok.

mei: good call. can we reproduce deterministically without batching? i already set batch=1, seed=42.

sachin: yes try forced single-head path: set opt.kernel_mode=reference in runtime config to force fallback kernel, see if it matches int8 baseline.

mei: did that — fallback matches baseline (dot preserved). so fast kernel + int4 quant path is the culprit.

ana: plan: 1) add targeted unit test for interpunct between han+hangul, 2) run quant parameter sweep (per-channel, clip thresholds), 3) short-term: disable fast-kernel for mixed-script tokens by heuristic, 4) longer-term: fix reorder in int4 kernel.

jun: I can add unit test and a small repro harness + curated examples (zh/ja/ko mixed) — pushing a PR in a bit.

mei: thanks. tagging @eng-ml for visibility. :eyes:

sachin: logging bug as INF-3245 and assigning to eng-ml-int4. ETA for hotfix? maybe next week if kernel fix; heuristic shim today.

ci-bot: INF-3245 created: https://issues.redwood.example/INF-3245

mei: perfect. i'll run the wider loc eval after the heuristic is in place and report BLEU diff in this thread.

ana: also let's add a simple synthetic test in the regression suite (two-token boundary with U+00B7 between scripts) so CI covers it.

jun: PR opened: https://git.redwood/eng-ml/orion/merge_requests/412 (unit tests + repro harness)

mei: great, closing loop for now — will post results once CI + sweep finish. :thumbsup:
